item_name: Staff Assessment of Resident Mood (PHQ-9-OV©) — H. Moving or speaking so slowly that other people have noticed. Or the opposite - being so fidgety or restless that they have been moving around a lot more than usual

lookback_source.quote: Conduct the interviews during the 7-day look-back period based on the ARD.

lookback_notes: The item's own pages state the staff interview is conducted during the 7-day look-back period based on the ARD (p. D-13). Counting follows the general convention of ARD plus the 6 previous calendar days (rai-manual-v1.20.1, p. 2-17: "ARD + 6 previous calendar days"). Note a second, different window is stated inside the interview itself: staff are asked about symptoms "Over the last 2 weeks" (p. D-12) and to "select how often over the past 2 weeks the symptom occurred" (p. D-15); the frequency codes are expressed in days out of 14. That symptom-recall period is recorded here and as a conflict, not as the assessor observation window.

coding_levels.label: Column 1, Symptom Presence — Code 0, no
coding_levels.definition: Symptom listed is not present; enter 0 in Column 2, Symptom Frequency.

source.quote: Code 0, no: if symptoms listed are not present. Enter 0 in Column 2, Symptom Frequency.

coding_levels.label: Column 1, Symptom Presence — Code 1, yes
coding_levels.definition: Symptom listed is present; enter 0, 1, 2, or 3 in Column 2, Symptom Frequency.

source.quote: Code 1, yes: if symptoms listed are present. Enter 0, 1, 2, or 3 in Column 2, Symptom Frequency.

coding_levels.label: Column 2, Symptom Frequency — Code 0, never or 1 day
coding_levels.definition: Staff indicate that the resident has never or has experienced the symptom on only 1 day.

source.quote: Code 0, never or 1 day: if staff indicate that the resident has never or has experienced the symptom on only 1 day.

coding_levels.label: Column 2, Symptom Frequency — Code 1, 2-6 days (several days)
coding_levels.definition: Staff indicate that the resident has experienced the symptom for 2-6 days.

source.quote: Code 1, 2-6 days (several days): if staff indicate that the resident has experienced the symptom for 2-6 days.

coding_levels.label: Column 2, Symptom Frequency — Code 2, 7-11 days (half or more of the days)
coding_levels.definition: Staff indicate that the resident has experienced the symptom for 7-11 days.

source.quote: Code 2, 7-11 days (half or more of the days): if staff indicate that the resident has experienced the symptom for 7-11 days.

coding_levels.label: Column 2, Symptom Frequency — Code 3, 12-14 days (nearly every day)
coding_levels.definition: Staff indicate that the resident has experienced the symptom for 12-14 days.

source.quote: Code 3, 12-14 days (nearly every day): if staff indicate that the resident has experienced the symptom for 12-14 days.

federal_coding_rules.rule: D0500 (including item H) is not conducted if the Resident Mood Interview (D0150–D0160) was completed.

source.quote: Do not conduct if Resident Mood Interview (D0150–D0160) was completed

federal_coding_rules.rule: The Staff Assessment of Resident Mood is completed only when D0100 is coded 0, No; it is not completed based on resident performance during the Resident Mood Interview.

source.quote: The assessor will complete the Staff Assessment only when D0100 is coded 0, No. The assessor does not complete the Staff Assessment based on resident performance during the Resident Mood Interview.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Do not complete the Staff Assessment of Resident Mood items (D0500) if the resident interview should have been conducted but was not done, or if the assessment being completed is a stand-alone Part A PPS Discharge assessment.

source.quote: Do not complete the Staff Assessment of Resident Mood items (D0500) if the resident interview should have been conducted but was not done, or if the assessment being completed is a stand-alone Part A PPS Discharge assessment.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If symptom frequency in D0150A2 through D0150I2 is blank or dashed for 3 or more items, the resident interview is deemed not complete, the Staff Assessment of Mood is not completed, and the assessor skips to D0700.

source.quote: If symptom frequency in items D0150A2 through D0150I2 is blank or dashed for 3 or more items, the interview is deemed NOT complete. Total Severity Score should be coded as "99," do not complete the Staff Assessment of Mood, and skip to D0700, Social Isolation.

federal_coding_rules.rule: The staff interviews for D0500 are conducted during the 7-day look-back period based on the ARD.

source.quote: Conduct the interviews during the 7-day look-back period based on the ARD.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Ask the staff member being interviewed to select how often over the past 2 weeks the symptom occurred, using the descriptive and/or numeric categories on the form.

source.quote: Ask the staff member being interviewed to select how often over the past 2 weeks the symptom occurred. Use the descriptive and/or numeric categories on the form (e.g., "nearly every day" or 3 = 12-14 days) to select a frequency response.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If a longer item (such as D0500H, which contains two phrases) was separated into its component parts, select the highest frequency rating that is reported.

source.quote: If you separated a longer item into its component parts, select the highest frequency rating that is reported.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If the staff member has difficulty selecting between two frequency responses, code for the higher frequency.

source.quote: If the staff member has difficulty selecting between two frequency responses, code for the higher frequency.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If the resident has been in the facility for less than 2 weeks, also talk to the family or significant other and review transfer records to inform selection of the frequency code.

source.quote: If the resident has been in the facility for less than 2 weeks, also talk to the family or significant other and review transfer records to inform selection of the frequency code.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Encourage staff to report symptom frequency even if the staff believes the symptom to be unrelated to depression.

source.quote: Encourage staff to report symptom frequency, even if the staff believes the symptom to be unrelated to depression.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Interview staff from all shifts who know the resident best, in a location that protects resident privacy.

source.quote: Interview staff from all shifts who know the resident best. Conduct the staff interview in a location that protects resident privacy.

federal_coding_rules.rule: D0500H frequency scores in Column 2 are added, together with the other D0500 items, into D0600 Total Severity Score (maximum 30); the interview is successfully completed if staff answered the frequency responses of at least 8 out of 10 items.

source.quote: The interview is successfully completed if the staff members were able to answer the frequency responses of at least 8 out of 10 items on the PHQ-9-OV©.

federal.criterion: Staff responses to D0500H such as "Their arthritis slows them down." or "They're bored and always looking for something to do." indicate a need for follow-up questioning with the staff member.

source.quote: D0500H, Moving or Speaking So Slowly That Other People Have Noticed. Or the Opposite—Being So Fidgety or Restless That They Have Been Moving Around a Lot More than Usual

federal.notes: Framed as examples of staff responses needing follow-up questioning, not as required documentation.

federal.criterion: When frequency cannot be determined by staff interview because the resident has been in the facility for less than 2 weeks, family/significant other input and transfer records are reviewed to inform the frequency code.

source.quote: If frequency cannot be determined by staff interview because the resident has been in the facility for less than 2 weeks, talk to family or significant other and review transfer records to inform the selection of a frequency code.

federal.notes: Stated as an assessment step; the pages do not state a chart-documentation requirement.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The supplied pages do not tie D0500H to any payment or case-mix classification.

conflicts.topic: Observation window for D0500H: 7-day look-back based on the ARD versus a 2-week symptom recall period built into the PHQ-9-OV© questions and frequency codes

positions.claim: The staff interviews for D0500 are to be conducted during the 7-day look-back period based on the ARD.

source.quote: Conduct the interviews during the 7-day look-back period based on the ARD.

positions.claim: The D0500 questions and frequency response categories ask about the last 2 weeks (0–14 days).

source.quote: Over the last 2 weeks, did the resident have any of the following problems or behaviors?

positions.claim: Coding tips direct the assessor to have staff select how often over the past 2 weeks the symptom occurred.

source.quote: Ask the staff member being interviewed to select how often over the past 2 weeks the symptom occurred.

conflicts.resolution: unresolved — surface to user. The 7-day window is the period in which the interview must be conducted; the 2-week period is the symptom-recall period asked of staff, but the pages do not explicitly reconcile the two.
